title: Buffalo Chicken Wings
subtitle: Crisp oven-baked wings in hot butter sauce
excerpt: Whole chicken wings roasted at high heat until the skin is very crisp, then tossed in a sharp, buttery hot sauce. Oven-baking rather than deep-frying gives you crackling skin without a vat of oil, and the method is far more manageable for a crowd. Serve with celery sticks and blue cheese dip if you like the full Buffalo experience.
sourceNotes: Buffalo wings were invented at the Anchor Bar in Buffalo, New York in 1964; the original sauce combined hot sauce with butter and became an American bar staple.

content.text: The secret to oven-crisp wings is a light dusting of flour before roasting on a rack. A wire rack set over a baking tray lets the heat circulate under the wings so the skin crisps all the way around rather than steaming on the bottom. If you don't have a rack, flip the wings halfway through. The sauce goes on at the very end, not in the oven, so the crisp skin stays intact.

items.prepNote: whole wings, tips removed if you prefer

content.text: Heat the oven to 220C (fan 200C / Gas 7). Pat the wings completely dry with kitchen paper. Moisture is the enemy of crisp skin, so take your time here.

Toss the wings in the flour, paprika, chilli flakes and a generous pinch of salt until evenly coated. Arrange on a wire rack set over a large baking tray, or directly on the tray in a single layer with space between each wing.
Roast for 40 to 45 minutes, turning once at the halfway point, until the skin is deeply golden and crisp. Internal temperature should reach 75C.
Meanwhile, melt the butter in a small pan over a low heat. Add the crushed garlic and cook for 1 minute. Stir in the Worcestershire sauce and honey. Season with salt. Keep warm on the lowest heat.
When the wings come out of the oven, tip them straight into a large bowl, pour over the sauce and toss well until every wing is coated. Serve immediately while the skin is still crackling.

items.cause: Wings were not dried thoroughly before coating, or they were overcrowded on the tray
items.fix: Next time pat very dry and use two trays rather than cramming them together. Steam has nowhere to escape when the wings are packed in.

items.symptom: Sauce is too thin and slides off
items.cause: Butter sauce was not reduced enough or wings were not hot enough when tossed
items.fix: Simmer the sauce for another 2 minutes to reduce it slightly before tossing. The wings must be piping hot from the oven for the sauce to cling.
